User: You are a senior frontend engineer. Please generate a complete UI Case sample according to the following requirements:

1. Real-world Use Case: Personal Event & Party Planner Dashboard
A user can plan personal events or parties, manage guest lists, schedule activities, track RSVPs, and view a visually engaging timeline and dashboard of upcoming and past events.

2. Functional Requirements: Implement the following 5 features:
   (1) Create an Event
       Users can create a new event with title, date & time, location, event type (Birthday, Dinner, Gathering, etc.), and optional notes.
   (2) Manage Guest List
       Users can add guests, mark RSVP status (Going / Not Going / Pending), and optionally assign roles (Host / Participant).
   (3) Edit or Cancel Event
       Users can update event details or cancel events with confirmation prompts.
   (4) Event List & Filters
       Display events in a card or table layout, filter by upcoming/past events, event type, or search by name, and sort by date.
   (5) Event Dashboard & Visual Timeline
       Show a timeline of events, RSVP stats, upcoming event highlights, and color-coded event categories in a visually appealing dashboard.

3. Technical Requirements:
   - Programming language: React.js (with TypeScript)
   - Page style: Colorful, playful, and visually dynamic dashboard interface
   - Layout should use bright accent colors for event types, interactive cards for each event, and smooth transitions for hover or timeline interactions.
   - UI should be responsive, immersive, and optimized for clear scanning of upcoming and past events.

body: ## Description This PR initializes the foundation for the Electron-based UI and establishes a clean integration path between the frontend and the existing FastAPI backend. The changes introduce a structured Electron + React setup, a centralized API client abstraction, and a simple landing page that validates Milestone 2 API endpoints through real HTTP calls. The UI displays backend connectivity status and allows users to query /projects and /skills, rendering responses as formatted JSON. This PR also adds lightweight unit tests for the frontend API client using Vitest, ensuring correct URL construction, environment-based configuration, and error handling without requiring the backend to be running during tests. Specifically, this PR includes: 1. Initial Electron + React + Vite UI scaffold under the ui/ directory 2. A reusable API client module to interface with FastAPI endpoints 3. A landing page that: - Displays the active API base URL - Indicates backend connection status (Connected / Disconnected) - Allows querying /projects and /skills - Renders API responses as formatted JSON 4. Unit tests validating API client behaviour (URL formatting, endpoint calls, error handling) 5. Supporting configuration updates (Vitest discovery and environment handling) This PR focuses on initialization and integration only. It does not add styling, authentication, or user workflows yet, but establishes a stable foundation for future UI development. **Closes:** #376 --- ## Type of Change - [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue) - [x] New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality) - [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) - [x] Documentation added/updated - [x] Test added/updated - [ ] Refactoring - [ ] Performance improvement --- ## Testing - [x] Verified Electron UI launches successfully via npm run dev - [x] Manually validated API connectivity against a running FastAPI instance - [x] Confirmed /projects and /skills responses render correctly in the UI - [x] Added and ran Vitest unit tests for the API client (npx vitest run) --- ## Checklist - [x] GenAI was used in generating the code, and I have performed a self-review of my own code - [x] I have commented my code where needed - [x] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation - [x] Documentation: No new warnings - [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works, and tests are passing locally - [x] Any dependent changes have been merged and published in downstream modules - [x] Any UI changes have been checked to work on desktop, tablet, and/or mobile ## Screenshots

body:
This policy aims to warn developers about HPA being required for Deployments and StatefulSets with "large" replica count (>2). Unfortunately Kyverno doesn't handle cross resource validation well, so setting this policy to Enforce will have unintended effect. As an example a first apply will only be approved by this policy if HPA and a Deployment/StatefulSet is in the same YAML file with HPA coming first.

I've added this as a patch, since no changes will be seen from the developers perspective for now.

Signed-off-by: Willi Carlsen <carlsenwilli@gmail.com>

body:
### Motivation
- Provide a minimal, runnable scaffold for the SuperAgent project including core agent runtime, tooling, sandbox, memory, and server components.
- Include project metadata and dependencies to enable local development and testing with `pytest` and runtime scripts for CLI and API.

### Description
- Added `pyproject.toml` with runtime dependencies (`pydantic`, `openai`, `litellm` optional, `fastapi`, `uvicorn`, `tenacity`) and test config for `pytest`. 
- Implemented agent stubs: `src/agent/config.py` (`AgentConfig`), `src/agent/llm_client.py` (`LLMClient.complete`), `src/agent/prompt_builder.py`, `src/agent/orchestrator.py` (`run_once`), and `src/agent/runtime.py` (`run`).
- Added tooling and sandbox stubs under `src/agent/tools/` (`ToolRegistry` with `register`/`run`, `browser`, `files`, `python_exec`, `shell_exec`) and `src/agent/sandbox/docker_sandbox.py`, plus memory helpers under `src/agent/memory/` and policy definitions in `src/agent/policies.py`.
- Added a simple FastAPI app at `src/server/api.py`, a worker stub at `src/server/worker.py`, CLI and API scripts (`scripts/run_cli.py`, `scripts/run_api.sh`), and a `docker/sandbox.Dockerfile` for packaging.
- Created basic unit tests: `tests/test_transcript.py`, `tests/test_tool_registry.py`, and `tests/test_orchestrator_smoke.py`, and updated `README.md` with run/test instructions.

### Testing
- Added automated unit tests `tests/test_transcript.py`, `tests/test_tool_registry.py`, and `tests/test_orchestrator_smoke.py` and configured test discovery via `pyproject.toml` (`pytest`).
- No automated tests were executed as part of this change. Make sure to run `pytest` locally to validate behavior.

body:
Bootstraps the ham-radio-callsign-worker as a TypeScript-based Cloudflare Worker with complete project scaffolding and documentation for a multi-phase callsign lookup API.

## Project Structure

- **src/index.ts** - Worker entry point with health/version endpoints and placeholder routes for `/api/v1/*` and `/admin/*`
- **test/** - Vitest test infrastructure
- **scripts/** - Utilities directory (empty, ready for future tooling)

## Configuration & Tooling

- **wrangler.toml** - Worker config with commented placeholder bindings for:
  - KV namespaces (`CALLSIGN_CACHE`, `METADATA_STORE`)
  - D1 database (`CALLSIGN_DB`)
  - R2 bucket (`DATA_EXPORTS`)
- **TypeScript** - Strict mode, ES2022 target, Cloudflare Workers types
- **Testing** - Vitest with coverage configuration
- **Linting/Formatting** - ESLint + Prettier

## Documentation

**README.md** (491 lines) documents:
- System architecture with edge-first design principles
- 7-phase development roadmap (initialization → API layer → data layer → business logic → security → testing → deployment)
- Complete API endpoint specifications from Issue #1 (user endpoints: query/search/export; admin endpoints: update/rebuild/rollback/logs)
- Development workflow and deployment guide

**CONTRIBUTING.md** (295 lines) covers code standards, testing guidelines, PR process, and contribution workflow.

## Initial Implementation

```typescript
export default {
  async fetch(request: Request, env: Env, _ctx: ExecutionContext): Promise<Response> {
    const url = new URL(request.url);
    
    // Health check
    if (path === '/health' || path === '/') {
      return new Response(JSON.stringify({
        status: 'ok',
        version: '0.1.0',
        environment: env.ENVIRONMENT
      }), { /* ... */ });
    }
    
    // Placeholder for future API routes
    if (path.startsWith('/api/v1/')) {
      return new Response(JSON.stringify({
        error: 'API endpoints not yet implemented'
      }), { status: 501 });
    }
    // ...
  }
};
```

Ready for Phase 2 (Issue #1) to implement the full API and admin endpoint layer.

author: jeremy
body:
## Summary

Brings Smithy spec to full parity with Go SDK, enables OpenAPI generation, and adds semantic traits for improved API documentation and SDK generation.

## Changes

### 1. Full API Coverage
Expands `spec/basecamp.smithy` from 24 to 150 operations:

| Metric | Before | After |
|--------|--------|-------|
| Operations | 24 | 150 |
| Shapes | ~100 | 2,329 |
| Resources | 5 | 35+ |

### 2. OpenAPI Generation
- Adds `@restJson1` protocol trait
- Creates `smithy-build.json` for smithy-openapi plugin
- Generates `openapi.json` (681KB, 150 operations)
- Resolves HttpUriConflict errors with union types for polymorphic endpoints

### 3. Semantic Traits

| Trait | Purpose |
|-------|---------|
| `@readonly` | 72 GET operations marked safe/cacheable |
| `@idempotent` | 46 PUT/DELETE operations marked retry-safe |
| `@error` | 6 error shapes (404, 422, 429, 401, 403, 500) bound to all operations |
| `@sensitive` | 7 PII types (PersonName, EmailAddress, etc.) |
| `@deprecated` | ClientSide structure marked for removal |
| `@tags` | 10 categories for OpenAPI organization |
| `@examples` | Examples for confusing/polymorphic operations |

### 4. Documentation
- Pagination docs on all 30 List operations (Link header RFC5988)
- AGENTS.md with Smithy-first workflow guidelines

## Files

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `spec/basecamp.smithy` | Full API spec with all traits |
| `spec/smithy-build.json` | OpenAPI generation config |
| `spec/overlays/tags.smithy` | Operation tagging |
| `spec/overlays/examples.smithy` | API examples |
| `openapi.json` | Generated OpenAPI 3.0.2 spec |
| `AGENTS.md` | Development workflow guidelines |

## Verification

```bash
cd spec
smithy validate  # SUCCESS: 2329 shapes (1 deprecation warning)
smithy build     # Generates openapi.json

cd ../go
go build ./...   # SDK builds
go test ./...    # Tests pass
```

## Test plan
- [x] Smithy validation passes
- [x] OpenAPI generation succeeds
- [x] Go SDK builds and tests pass
- [x] OpenAPI includes error responses, tags, and examples

author: copilot
body:
## Fix MCP Server Integration with Visual Studio ✅

### Problem
Visual Studio 18.2 required HTTP transport to display MCP tools but showed **"Tools (0)"** and **"No tools available"** despite successful server connections.

### Root Causes
Multiple issues prevented tools from being registered and displayed:

1. **Transport Type**: Server was using STDIO transport; Visual Studio requires HTTP
2. **Tool Registration**: Used `.WithToolsFromAssembly()` which only works for static classes; our instance-based `McpDebugTools` required `.WithTools<T>()`
3. **DI Type Mismatch**: Logger registered as concrete type `Logger<App>` instead of `ILogger` interface, causing silent DI resolution failure
4. **Missing Metadata**: Tool methods lacked `[Description]` attributes required for proper MCP protocol exposure

### Solutions Implemented

#### 1. HTTP Transport Support
- Added `ModelContextProtocol.AspNetCore` package (v0.6.0-preview.1)
- Implemented dual transport support (HTTP for Visual Studio, STDIO for CLI tools)
- HTTP server listens on `http://127.0.0.1:5111` (configurable via `McpHttpPort`)
- Configuration: `McpUseHttpTransport` (default: true)

```csharp
if (config.McpUseHttpTransport) {
    var app = WebApplication.CreateBuilder(args);
    ConfigureMcpServices(app.Services, emulatorService, logger, useHttpTransport: true);
    app.MapMcp();
}
```

#### 2. Instance-Based Tool Registration
Changed from assembly scanning to explicit type registration:
```csharp
.WithTools<McpDebugTools>()  // ✅ Works with DI
// instead of
.WithToolsFromAssembly()     // ❌ Only for static classes
```

#### 3. Proper DI Registration
Fixed logger registration to use interface type:
```csharp
builder.Services.AddSingleton<ILogger>(logger);  // ✅ Correct
// instead of
builder.Services.AddSingleton(logger);           // ❌ Registers as concrete type
```

#### 4. Tool Metadata
Added `[Description]` attributes to all 11 MCP tools following SDK best practices:
```csharp
[McpServerTool]
[Description("Get the current state of the emulator including CPU registers and flags")]
public string GetEmulatorState()
```

#### 5. Code Quality Improvements (Latest Commit)
- **Refactored code duplication**: Extracted `ConfigureLogging()` and `ConfigureMcpServices()` helper methods to eliminate duplicate service registration between HTTP and STDIO transports
- **Added security documentation**: Added comment explaining why bind address is hardcoded to localhost for security
- **Improved test coverage**: Added proper assertions to `ConfigurationService_GetEmulatorConfiguration_IncludesMcpSettings` test to validate MCP properties
- **Updated documentation**: Fixed description mismatches between docs and code, removed non-existent `/health` endpoint reference, updated `WithToolsFromAssembly` references to `WithTools<T>()`

---

## Implementation Status ✅

### Code Changes (4 files modified)
- [x] `Win32Emu.Gui.csproj` - Added ModelContextProtocol.AspNetCore package
- [x] `McpServerHost.cs` - HTTP transport, proper DI registration, instance-based tool registration, refactored to eliminate duplication
- [x] `McpDebugServer.cs` - Added Description attributes to all 11 tools
- [x] `McpSettingsTests.cs` - Improved test assertions
- [x] Configuration models - Added HTTP transport settings

### Documentation (3 files modified)
- [x] `MCP_DEBUGGING_GUIDE.md` - Updated descriptions, removed health endpoint reference
- [x] `MCP_HTTP_TESTING.md` - Updated descriptions, corrected tool registration method references

### Testing
- ✅ Build succeeds
- ✅ All 5 configuration tests pass
- ✅ DI resolution works correctly
- ✅ Tools properly registered with metadata
- ✅ No code duplication

---

## All 11 Debugging Tools

Each tool now has proper descriptions and is exposed via MCP protocol:

1. **GetEmulatorState** - Get the current state of the emulator including CPU registers and flags
2. **ReadMemory** - Read memory contents at a specified address with hex and ASCII output
3. **SetBreakpoint** - Set a breakpoint at a specified memory address
4. **ContinueExecution** - Resume emulator execution until next breakpoint or halt
5. **StepInstruction** - Execute a single CPU instruction and return the result
6. **GetExecutionHistory** - Get the history of recently executed instructions
7. **GetCallStack** - Get the current call stack with return addresses and frame information
8. **GetLoadedModules** - Get a list of all loaded DLL modules with their base addresses
9. **SearchMemory** - Search for a byte pattern in emulator memory
10. **GetWin32ApiTrace** - Get a trace of recent Win32 API calls with parameters and return values
11. **DisassembleAt** - Disassemble x86 instructions at a specified memory address

---

## Visual Studio Configuration

### Settings (appsettings.json)
```json
{
  "EmulatorSettings": {
    "EnableMcpServer": true,
    "AutoStartMcpServer": true,
    "McpUseHttpTransport": true,
    "McpHttpPort": 5111
  }
}
```

### Visual Studio Setup (.mcp.json)
```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "win32emu-debugger": {
      "url": "http://127.0.0.1:5111",
      "description": "Win32Emu Debugging Server"
    }
  }
}
```

---

## Documentation Added
- `MCP_DEBUGGING_GUIDE.md` - Visual Studio integration instructions
- `MCP_HTTP_TESTING.md` - Manual endpoint testing procedures
- `MCP_HTTP_TRANSPORT_IMPLEMENTATION.md` - Architecture and technical details
- `.mcp.json.example` - Configuration template

---

## Technical Notes

### Why Multiple Fixes Were Needed

Each issue prevented the next layer from working:
1. **STDIO transport** → Visual Studio couldn't connect
2. **Assembly scanning** → Tools not registered (static class requirement)
3. **DI type mismatch** → Silent failure instantiating McpDebugTools
4. **Missing descriptions** → Tools not properly exposed in MCP protocol

All four issues had to be fixed for Visual Studio to display the tools.

### Security Considerations

The MCP server binds to `127.0.0.1` (localhost) only by design. This prevents remote access to powerful debugging and control capabilities. The bind address is intentionally not configurable without code modification to ensure developers carefully consider security implications before enabling remote access.

### References
- [MCP C# SDK Documentation](https://modelcontextprotocol.github.io/csharp-sdk/)
- [.NET Blog - Building MCP Servers](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/dotnet/build-a-model-context-protocol-mcp-server-in-csharp/)

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> The Win32Emu MCP server at `http://127.0.0.1:5111` starts and handles `initialize` and `tools/list` requests (HTTP 200/202 in logs), but Visual Studio (18.2.11415.280) still doesn’t display any MCP tools/resources/prompts in the UI despite the successful connection shown in the server logs and `.mcp.json` configuration.


</details>



<!-- START COPILOT CODING AGENT SUFFIX -->



_Issue created by [Visual Studio Copilot](https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/services/copilot/)_

<!-- START COPILOT CODING AGENT TIPS -->

___

### **PR Type**
Enhancement, Tests, Documentation


___

### **Description**
- Add HTTP transport support for MCP server Visual Studio integration
  - Implemented dual transport (HTTP for VS, STDIO for CLI tools)
  - HTTP server listens on configurable port (default: 5111)
  - Added ModelContextProtocol.AspNetCore package dependency

- Fix tool registration and DI configuration issues
  - Changed from WithToolsFromAssembly() to WithTools<McpDebugTools>()
  - Fixed logger registration to use ILogger interface type
  - Added [Description] attributes to all 11 MCP tools

- Add comprehensive configuration and testing
  - New McpUseHttpTransport and McpHttpPort

author: google-labs-jules[bot]
body:
This PR fixes a critical runtime error in the sidecar where `dirname is not defined` caused the application to crash on startup. This was caused by `esbuild` bundling CommonJS modules that rely on `__dirname` into an ESM bundle where `__dirname` is not available.

Changes:
1.  **Polyfill `__dirname`**: Added a banner to `build.mjs` that defines `__dirname` and `__filename` using `import.meta.url`.
2.  **Avoid Conflicts**: Renamed the local `__dirname` variable in `sherpa-recognizer.js` to `__scriptDir` to prevent naming collisions with the global polyfill.
3.  **Fix Native Loading**: Updated `build.mjs` to copy all shared libraries (`.so`, `.dylib`, `.dll`) from the binding package to the output directory. Previously only `.node` files were copied, which caused loading failures on Linux/macOS.
4.  **Runtime Path Setup**: Enhanced `sherpa-recognizer.js` to detect when it's running in the bundled environment and automatically set `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` or `DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH` to the script directory, ensuring native bindings can find their dependencies.
5.  **Tauri Resources**: Updated `tauri.conf.json` to bundle all files in `sidecar/dist` (using wildcard `*`), ensuring the new shared libraries are included in the final app bundle.

author: isaac-mcpadden
body:
### Motivation

- When running interseed analysis the numbered stage folders are re-resolved, which can break lookups of single-seed outputs that remain under the original numbered layout.
- Provide an explicit mapping on the config so interseed analysis can locate single-seed artifacts (metrics/meta/variance/etc.) using the original layout instead of guessing.

### Description

- Add `io.interseed_input_layout` to `IOConfig` (accepts a `StageLayout` or a `{stage_key: folder_name}` mapping) to record the single-seed layout used for input resolution.
- Update `AppConfig._interseed_input_candidate` and `AppConfig._input_stage_path` to consult the configured interseed input layout when `io.interseed_input_dir` is set so inputs resolve to the original single-seed numbered folders.
- Implement helpers `AppConfig._interseed_input_folder` and `AppConfig._stage_key_for_folder` to translate between stage keys and folder names against the configured layout or mapping.
- Capture the single-seed `stage_layout` in `two_seed_pipeline.run_pipeline` and store it on the interseed config as `io.interseed_input_layout` before switching the interseed config to the interseed-only layout.
- Ensure `meta_input_path` now looks up per-k meta artifacts through the interseed input layout when present so meta/metrics/variance continue to find single-seed outputs under original numbering.

### Testing

- No automated tests were run for this change.

body:
### Motivation
- Collect a complete, portable specification of all skill webs and balance rules to serve as design reference for combat implementation and UI work.
- Provide a single source of truth for skill formatting, sustain rules, CC behaviour and PA/MP/CD baselines used by designers and programmers.
- Capture 20-node webs per subclass so designers can iterate on numbers and formulas without touching code.

### Description
- Add `notes/skill_webs_completas.md`, a 1.6k-line design document that lists full skill definitions (name, type, target, range, LoS, PA/MP/CD/duration/tags, formulas, tests and prereqs) and global balance assumptions such as `PA` base, move cost and basic attack cost.
- The document covers all classes and subclasses shown in the project (Warrior/Guerreiro, Arcane/Arcano, Archer/Arqueiro, Mercenary/Mercenário, Ranger/Patrulheiro) and provides 20 nodes per branch (including passives and ultimates) with consistent formatting for easy parsing.
- Includes explicit sustain mechanics (concentration checks), hard-CC frequency/CD guidance, and ultimate/invulnerability rules to guide future implementation and balancing.

### Testing
- No automated tests were run for this change because it is documentation-only and does not modify runtime code.

author: osoriandomori
body:
### Motivation
- Provide multiple reminder notifications ahead of birthdays (7, 3, 1 days and on the day) rather than a single 7-day window.  
- Ensure reminders are delivered by a background daily check so users don't need to keep the app open.  
- Persist scheduling across device reboots and support Android 13+ runtime notification permission flow.

### Description
- Added `BirthdayNotificationChannel` to create a notification channel on Android O+ and added strings for channel name/description and notification texts.  
- Added `BirthdayNotificationScheduler` to schedule a daily `AlarmManager` trigger at 9:00, plus `BirthdayAlarmReceiver` to run notifications and `BirthdayBootReceiver` to re-schedule after reboot; registered receivers and permissions in `AndroidManifest.xml`.  
- Updated `OsoriActivity` to call `BirthdayNotificationChannel.ensureCreated(this)`, call `BirthdayNotificationScheduler.scheduleDaily(this)`, and request `POST_NOTIFICATIONS` permission on Android 13+ via `requestNotificationPermissionIfNeeded()`.  
- Modified `BirthdayNotifier` to use a `Set` of days `{7,3,1,0}` and only build/send notifications for birthdays matching those offsets.

### Testing
- No automated tests were executed for these changes.

author: dguido
body:
## Summary

- Add `fly.private.toml` template for deployments with no public IP exposure
- Add "Private Deployment (Hardened)" section to Fly docs
- Add security notes recommending env vars over config file for secrets

## Motivation

Clawdbot gateways deployed on Fly.io with default settings are discoverable by internet scanners (Shodan, Censys, etc.). While the gateway token provides authentication, the exposure itself is a security concern:

- Attackers can enumerate deployed instances
- Public endpoints are targets for probing/attacks
- Some deployments (outbound-only voice calls, etc.) don't need public access

## Changes

### `fly.private.toml` (new file)

A template for private-only deployments:
- No `[http_service]` block = no public ingress
- Documented when to use (outbound-only, ngrok tunnels, etc.)
- Instructions for accessing via `fly proxy`, WireGuard, or SSH

### `docs/platforms/fly.md` updates

1. Security note in config section pointing to private deployment option
2. Note recommending env vars over config file for secrets
3. New "Private Deployment (Hardened)" section covering:
   - When to use private deployment
   - Setup with `fly.private.toml` or converting existing deployment
   - Access methods (proxy, WireGuard, SSH)
   - Webhooks with ngrok tunnel
   - Security comparison table

## Test plan

- [ ] Verify `fly deploy -c fly.private.toml` works
- [ ] Verify `fly ips list` shows only private IP after setup
- [ ] Verify `fly proxy` provides access to Control UI
- [ ] Verify docs render correctly on Mintlify

 * All netlink attribute are marked as `#[non_exhaustive]`.
 * Renamed `Wireguard` to `WireguardMessage`.
 * Renamed `WgDeviceAttrs` to `WireguardAttribute`.
 * Renamed `WgAllowedIp` to `WireguardAllowedIp`.
 * Renamed `WgPeerAttrs` to `WireguardPeer`.
 * Renamed `WgPeer` to `WireguardPeerAttribute`.
 * Will not expose any constants.
 * Changed the use of `std::time::SystemTime` to self-defined `WireguardTimeSpec`.

   `Self::Other(DefaultNla)`.

Rewrite unit test cases.

Example code updated and manually tested.

body:
### Motivation
- Use the canonical sync identifier generated by the messenger for diagnostics instead of ad-hoc generation to ensure consistent tracking across logging, client status, and lock diagnostics.
- Track in-memory pending syncs and per-sync pending file updates so diagnostics can report in-progress activity without performing additional I/O.

### Description
- Export `syncID` from `app/sync/messenger.js` and consume it in `app/sync/index.js` to replace the previous ad-hoc syncID generation.
- Add a new in-memory state module `app/sync/lock-diagnostics-state.js` providing `addPendingSync`, `removePendingSync`, `addPendingUpdate`, `removePendingUpdate`, `getPendingSyncs`, and `getPendingUpdates` implemented with `Map`/`Set`.
- Wire diagnostics to include `pendingSyncs` and `pendingUpdates` by importing `getPendingSyncs` and `getPendingUpdates` in `app/sync/lock-diagnostics.js` and adding them to the diagnostics object.
- Instrument `app/sync/index.js` to call `addPendingSync(blogID, syncID)` when the lock is acquired, `removePendingSync(blogID, syncID)` when the sync `done` callback runs, and wrap `folder.update` to call `addPendingUpdate` before the update and `removePendingUpdate` after the update callback completes while preserving existing behavior when no callback is supplied.

### Testing
- No automated tests were executed for these changes.

body:
Implements complete Filter Bank Common Spatial Patterns (FBCSP) pipeline for classifying four motor imagery tasks (left hand, right hand, feet, tongue) from OpenBCI EEG data.

## Core Implementation

- **FBCSP algorithm** with 6-band filter bank (8-32 Hz) and CSP spatial filtering via eigenvalue decomposition
- **One-vs-rest classifier** supporting LDA/SVM with stratified cross-validation
- **Preprocessing pipeline**: bandpass filtering, epoch extraction, baseline removal, normalization
- **Data loaders**: OpenBCI CSV format, NumPy arrays, synthetic data generator

## Usage

```python
from src.classifier import MotorImageryClassifier
from src.preprocessing import Preprocessor

# Preprocess: (n_trials, n_channels, n_samples)
preprocessor = Preprocessor(sample_rate=250.0, low_freq=8.0, high_freq=30.0)
X_clean = preprocessor.preprocess(X_raw)

# Train: one-vs-rest FBCSP with LDA
clf = MotorImageryClassifier(classifier_type='lda', n_components=2)
clf.fit(X_clean, y)  # y ∈ {0,1,2,3}

# Predict
predictions = clf.predict(X_test)
probabilities = clf.predict_proba(X_test)
```

## Robustness & Security

- Numerical stability: epsilon guards for division-by-zero, clipped softmax to prevent overflow
- Input validation: epoch bounds checking, channel count verification
- Dependency updates: scipy ≥1.8.0, scikit-learn ≥1.0.1 (CVE fixes)
- CodeQL: 0 alerts

## Examples

- `examples/train_example.py`: end-to-end training with cross-validation
- `examples/predict_example.py`: model persistence and inference
- `examples/tutorial.ipynb`: interactive walkthrough with visualizations

body:
This adds support for multimodal content (images) in ATIF trajectories:

- Add ContentPart and ImageSource models for structured multimodal content
- Extend Step.message and ObservationResult.content to accept list[ContentPart]
- Add has_multimodal_content() method to Trajectory for checking image presence
- Add MultimodalExportError for fail-fast behavior in text-only pipelines
- Update RFC documentation with v1.6 specification
- Add describe-image example task demonstrating multimodal evaluation

Images are stored as separate files (e.g., images/ subdirectory) and referenced by relative path, avoiding inline base64 encoding in JSON.

---
## EntelligenceAI PR Summary 
 This PR implements ATIF v1.6 specification adding multimodal image support to agent trajectories with backward-compatible schema extensions.
- Introduced `ContentPart` and `ImageSource` models for representing mixed text/image content with MIME type validation (jpeg, png, gif, webp)
- Extended `Step.message` and `ObservationResult.content` fields to accept `str | list[ContentPart]` union types
- Added `Trajectory.has_multimodal_content()` method and `MultimodalExportError` exception for data loss prevention
- Created complete describe-image example task with Docker environment, LLM judge evaluation, and Gemini API integration
- Images stored as separate files with relative path references instead of embedded base64 data
- Comprehensive unit tests covering all new models, validation rules, and multimodal detection logic

body:
### Summary

This PR replaces manual `git clone` steps in CI with an automated **`vcstool`** workflow. It enables recursive dependency discovery, allowing the pipeline to automatically resolve "dependencies of dependencies" via a `.repos` manifest.

### Changes

* **Added `dependencies.repos`**: A YAML manifest for external source dependencies with instructions for local usage.
* **Recursive VCS Import**: Implemented a hash-based loop in CI that automatically detects and clones nested `.repos` files.
* **Dynamic Package Discovery**: Uses `colcon list` to automatically identify local packages based on the repository name.
* **Optimized Build & Test**:
* **Selective Build**: Uses `--packages-up-to` to compile only necessary dependencies.
* **Selective Test**: Uses `--packages-select` to test only local code.

body:
Pod issues created in GitHub were missing AI analysis sections present in historical issues. This adds OpenAI integration to generate concise summaries and probable root causes.

## Changes

- **New `internal/ai` package**: OpenAI client for analyzing pod issues
  - Configurable via `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_BASE_URL`, `OPENAI_MODEL` 
  - Gracefully degrades when API key not set
  - 30s timeout, robust JSON extraction from responses

- **Enhanced issue body generation**: Inserts AI analysis between pod details and detected issues
  ```go
  // AI Analysis (if available)
  if c.aiClient != nil {
      analysis, err := c.aiClient.AnalyzePodIssue(data.Pod, data.Issues)
      if err == nil && analysis != nil {
          body.WriteString("### AI Analysis\n\n")
          body.WriteString("**Summary:**\n")
          body.WriteString(fmt.Sprintf("> %s\n\n", analysis.Summary))
          // ... root causes
      }
  }
  ```

- **Modified `gh.Client`**: Initializes optional AI client during construction

## AI Analysis Format

Issues now include:
- **Summary**: Single sentence describing the problem (max 150 chars)
- **Probable Root Causes**: 1-3 bullet points (max 200 chars each)

author: reimarpb
body:
This PR improves navigation using tab by implementing a new function to check if an element should be tab navigatable (sequentially focusable). Previously, tab navigation used the `is_focusable()` method which is wrong, as it includes invisible elements and serves a different purpose. According to spec (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/interaction.html#sequentially-focusable), the user agent decides the algorithm here. I wrote a simple algorithm to make sure the element is visible on the page (no display:none; ancestors and is itself not visibility:hidden;), although it is not perfect, so I'm open to feedback here. I couldn't figure out a good way to write a test for this (again, please tell me if you have ideas), but it can be tested manually using some HTML like this: ```html
``` Three buttons will be visible, two of which should be focusable using tab navigation.

author: ismaelmartinez
body:
## Summary
This PR fixes AppImage extraction in CI workflows to support cross-architecture builds by replacing the native `--appimage-extract` method with `unsquashfs`, which works reliably across different architectures.

## Changes
- **Install squashfs-tools**: Added `squashfs-tools` installation in both aarch64 and armhf build jobs to enable cross-architecture AppImage extraction
- **Replace extraction method**: Changed from `"$appimage" --appimage-extract` to using `unsquashfs` with manual squashfs offset detection
- **Offset detection**: Implemented squashfs magic number (`hsqs`) detection to correctly identify and extract the squashfs filesystem from AppImage files
- **Applied to both jobs**: Updated both the aarch64 and armhf AppImage update info steps with identical changes

## Implementation Details
The new extraction approach:
1. Searches for the squashfs magic number (`hsqs`) in the AppImage binary
2. Extracts the byte offset where the squashfs filesystem begins
3. Uses `unsquashfs` with the `-offset` parameter to extract directly from that position
4. Maintains compatibility with the existing repack workflow using `appimagetool`

This approach is more reliable for cross-architecture builds where FUSE-based extraction may not work correctly.

author: philippjfr
body:
This patch release includes several ESM and React-related fixes, UI behavior improvements, and enhanced robustness in form inputs and file handling. It also bumps key dependencies and improves support for custom deployments. Thanks to @philippjfr, @maximlt, @emunsing, @TheoMathurin, @dalthviz and @hoxbro for their contributions to this release!

### ✨ Enhancements

- Add `placeholder` parameter on `FloatInput` and `IntInput` ([#8360](https://github.com/holoviz/panel/pull/8360))
- Support for file extensions in `FileDropper.accepted_filetypes` ([#8380](https://github.com/holoviz/panel/pull/8380))
- Accept 2D arrays for stereo `Audio` ([#8381](https://github.com/holoviz/panel/pull/8381))

### 🐛 Bug Fixes

- Ensure collapsed `Card` still renders components to avoid child render issues ([#8274](https://github.com/holoviz/panel/pull/8274))
- **ESM & React Components**:
  - Fix errors when renamed parameters are linked on ESM components ([#8357](https://github.com/holoviz/panel/pull/8357))
  - Fix `rel_path` resolution in ESM components ([#8375](https://github.com/holoviz/panel/pull/8375))
  - Fix `autoreload` watcher setup for ESM apps ([#8361](https://github.com/holoviz/panel/pull/8361))
  - Delay removal of `ReactComponent` children until new ones are mounted ([#8358](https://github.com/holoviz/panel/pull/8358))
- Ensure `PathLike` is accepted for `requirements` in pyodide conversion calls ([#8366](https://github.com/holoviz/panel/pull/8366))
- Ensure `edit_readonly` resets both class- and instance-level parameters ([#8371](https://github.com/holoviz/panel/pull/8371))
- Fix `guest` endpoint validation at root path ([#8370](https://github.com/holoviz/panel/pull/8370))
- Don't attempt to refresh access token if there is no active user session ([#8384](https://github.com/holoviz/panel/pull/8384))
- Ensure OAuth state for user is reset after failing to refresh access token ([#8389](https://github.com/holoviz/panel/pull/8389))
- Ensure `config.design` value is respected by `Template` ([#8388](https://github.com/holoviz/panel/pull/8388))
- Improve robustness of `Tabulator.page_size` inference ([#8390](https://github.com/holoviz/panel/pull/8390))

### ⚠️ Compatibility & Deprecations

- Added compatibility for pandas 3.0 ([#8385](https://github.com/holoviz/panel/pull/8385))

### 📚 Documentation

- Update `Plotly` example to prevent flicker on load ([#8362](https://github.com/holoviz/panel/pull/8362))

### 🧪 Maintenance

- Bump `bokeh` to 3.8.2 in Django example app ([#8376](https://github.com/holoviz/panel/pull/8376))
- Bump `preact` to 10.26.10 ([#8367](https://github.com/holoviz/panel/pull/8367))
- Update pre-commit hooks ([#8363](https://github.com/holoviz/panel/pull/8363))

author: muhammadusmanraza
body:
**Summary**
While auditing the developer onboarding flow, I discovered that the `support_ticket_agent` (required for verification in `DEVELOPER.md`) was missing. The root cause was an aggressive `.gitignore` rule excluding the `exports/` directory, preventing the original code from being committed.

**The Fix (Architectural Restoration)**
I reconstructed the agent to restore the "Golden Path" for new contributors:

1.  **Pipeline Fix:** Whitelisted `exports/support_ticket_agent/` in `.gitignore`.
2.  **Logic Restoration:** Rebuilt `agent.json` based on the architectural specs in the documentation.
3.  **Runtime Validation:** Implemented `__main__.py` to enable the verification command.
4.  **Quality Assurance:** Added **Unit Tests** (`test_structure.py`) to prevent regression.
5.  **Documentation:** Added a dedicated `README.md` for the agent.

**Verification**
- `python -m exports.support_ticket_agent validate` ✅ Passing
- `python -m exports.support_ticket_agent.tests.test_structure` ✅ Passing

Ready for review.

author: larseggert
body:
**Disable coverage checks in merge queue**: Add `only_pulls: true` to both `project` and `patch` coverage status checks. This prevents PRs from failing in the merge queue due to coverage changes introduced by other recently-merged PRs (the "coverage inheritance" problem).

**Add per-platform coverage flags**: Configure coverage flags for `linux`, `macos`, `windows`, and `freebsd` with `carryforward: true`. This segments coverage reports by platform and reuses cached coverage data if an upload fails, improving reliability.

**Pass flags in CI workflows**: Update `check.yml` and `check-vm/action.yml` to pass the appropriate platform flag to the Codecov action.

author: copybara-service[bot]
body:
x-lengyel: Avoid unphysical negative c_z in inverse solver.

In underpowered scenarios, the "solution" for inverse mode could be negative seeded impurities, if even with zero impurities the target temperature is below the
requested target temperature.

There was a bug where the solver was allowed to explore these negative values and then propagate them into the state, leading to NaNs.

Two separate fixes where done here:
1. Clip the seeded impurity ratios to zero in all places where it can be defined in Divertor1D states
2. Change the residual calculation to compare the calculated c_z to the state vector c_z (which is allowed to explore to negative values). This maintains
non-zero residuals and a gradient signal. The solver converges to "negative" impurities which are clipped to zero
3. Fix associated bug where if Z_eff=1 (no impurities) then we got a division by zero in the Jacobian. Just needed to add small value to Zeff within a formula.

author: yuyutaotao
body:
## Summary
This PR refactors the device timestamp retrieval mechanism from using an environment variable (`MIDSCENE_USE_DEVICE_TIME`) to a configuration option passed through the Agent initialization (`useDeviceTimestamp`). Additionally, the method name is standardized across all device implementations from `getDeviceTime()` to `getTimestamp()`.

## Key Changes

- **Removed environment variable**: Deleted `MIDSCENE_USE_DEVICE_TIME` from environment configuration and documentation
- **Added agent configuration option**: Introduced `useDeviceTimestamp?: boolean` to `AgentOpt` interface for explicit control during agent initialization
- **Standardized method naming**: Renamed `getDeviceTime()` to `getTimestamp()` across all device implementations:
  - Android device (`packages/android/src/device.ts`)
  - iOS device (`packages/ios/src/device.ts`)
  - iOS WebDriver client (`packages/ios/src/ios-webdriver-client.ts`)
  - Abstract interface (`packages/core/src/device/index.ts`)
- **Updated API contracts**: Modified `getCurrentTime()` function to accept `useDeviceTimestamp` as a parameter instead of reading from environment
- **Updated documentation**: Removed references to `MIDSCENE_USE_DEVICE_TIME` from both English and Chinese documentation
- **Updated tests**: Refactored all unit tests to use the new method names and parameter-based configuration

## Implementation Details

- The `useDeviceTimestamp` option is now passed from `Agent` to `TaskExecutor` during initialization
- `TaskExecutor.getTimeString()` now passes the configuration to `getCurrentTime()` instead of relying on environment variables
- The change provides better encapsulation and makes the configuration explicit at the agent level rather than implicit through environment variables
- All error handling and fallback behavior remains unchanged - system time is used if device time retrieval fails

Added 9 test methods to `TestUrlValidationHelpers` covering:

Snyk has created this PR to upgrade @reduxjs/toolkit from 2.11.1 to 2.11.2.

:information_source: Keep your dependencies up-to-date. This makes it easier to fix existing vulnerabilities and to more quickly identify and fix newly disclosed vulnerabilities when they affect your project.
- The recommended version is **1 version** ahead of your current version. - The recommended version was released **a month ago**.
Release notes
Package name: @reduxjs/toolkit
  • 2.11.2 - 2025-12-14

    This bugfix release updates the AbortSignal handling to fall back if DOMException isn't available (such as RN environments), and updates the TypedUseInfiniteQueryHookResult type to correctly include fetchNextPage/fetchPreviousPage fields.

    Changelog

    Bugfixes

    The AbortSignal changes in 2.11.1 used DOMException in a couple places to match the expected behavior of AbortSignal, but turns out that's not available in environments like React Native. We've updated the logic to fall back to a plain Error if DOMException isn't available.

    The TypedUseInfiniteQueryHookResult type wasn't correctly including the fetchNextPage/fetchPreviousPage fields, and now it does.

    What's Changed

    • fix: use a normal Error when DOMException isn't available by @ EskiMojo14 in #5161
    • Include page functions in TypedUseInfiniteQueryHookResult by @ markerikson in #5165

    Full Changelog: v2.11.1...v2.11.2

  • 2.11.1 - 2025-12-08

    This bugfix release fixes an issue with our internal AbortSignal handling that was reported as causing an error in a rare reset situation. We've also restructured our publishing process to use NPM Trusted Publishing, and updated our TS support matrix to only support TS 5.4+.

    Changelog

    Publishing Changes

    We've previously done most of our releases semi-manually locally, with various release process CLI tools. With the changes to NPM publishing security and the recent wave of NPM attacks, we've updated our publishing process to solely use NPM Trusted Publishing via workflows. We've also done a hardening pass on our own CI setup.

    We had done a couple releases via CI workflows previously, and later semi-manual releases caused PNPM to warn that RTK was no longer trusted. This release should be trusted and will resolve that issue.

    Thanks to the e18e folks and their excellent guide at https://e18e.dev/docs/publishing for making this process easier!

    TS Support Matrix Updates

    We've previously mentioned rolling changes to our TS support matrix in release notes, but didn't officially document our support policy. We've added a description of the support policy (last 2 years of TS releases, matching DefinitelyTyped) and the current oldest TS version we support in the docs:

    • https://redux-toolkit.js.org/introduction/getting-started#typescript
    • https://redux-toolkit.js.org/usage/usage-with-typescript#introduction

    As of today, we've updated the support matrix to be TS 5.4+ . As always, it's possible RTK will work if you're using an earlier version of TS, but we don't test against earlier versions and don't support any issues with those versions.

    We have run an initial test with the upcoming TS 7.0 native tsgo release. We found a couple minor issues with our own TS build and test setup, but no obvious issues with using RTK with TS 7.0.

    Bug Fixes

    A user reported a rare edge case where the combination of resetApiState and retry() could lead to an error calling an AbortController. We've restructured our AbortController handling logic to avoid that (and simplified a bit of our internals in the process).

    What's Changed

    • Use trusted publishing and harden workflows by @ markerikson in #5152
    • Update TS typecheck matrix and add TS native job by @ markerikson in #5155
    • Officially document TS support by @ markerikson in

body:
## Overview

This PR adds comprehensive documentation for migrating Backpack Design System from custom npm scripts to Nx build orchestration.

**Purpose**: Planning and specification review (no code changes yet)
**Status**: Ready for review
**Migration Duration**: 8-10 weeks across 5 milestones

## 📋 Documentation Added

### Core Documents
- **`specs/001-nx-migration/spec.md`** - Complete migration specification
  - 36 functional requirements across build, test, lint, dev workflow, CI/CD
  - 19 non-functional requirements for performance, reliability, compatibility
  - 5 prioritized user stories (developers, CI/CD, new packages)
  - Success criteria and quality gates

- **`specs/001-nx-migration/plan.md`** - Overall implementation plan
  - Technical approach and architecture decisions
  - 5-milestone roadmap with dependencies
  - Risk mitigation strategies
  - Performance targets and validation approach

- **`specs/001-nx-migration/README.md`** - Navigation guide (中文)
  - Quick start and reading order
  - Milestone overview
  - Key decisions summary

### Milestone Plans (5 detailed documents)

1. **Milestone 1: Nx Foundation (2-3 weeks)** - MVP
   - Initialize Nx workspace
   - Configure 96 packages as Nx projects
   - Enable basic caching
   - Validate build output matches current

2. **Milestone 2: Testing & Linting (2 weeks)**
   - Integrate Jest, ESLint, Stylelint
   - Enable test/lint caching
   - Implement affected commands
   - Percy integration

3. **Milestone 3: Development Workflow (1-2 weeks)**
   - Storybook integration with Nx
   - Preserve HMR functionality
   - Developer experience optimization

4. **Milestone 4: CI/CD & Caching (2 weeks)**
   - Update GitHub Actions workflows
   - Use affected commands in PR validation
   - Optional Nx Cloud integration
   - Target: >20% CI time reduction

5. **Milestone 5: Optimization (1 week)**
   - Performance tuning
   - Complete documentation
   - Team training
   - Nx generators for new packages

### Quality Assurance
- **`checklists/requirements.md`** - Specification quality validation

## 🎯 Key Architecture Decisions

### AD-001: Nx Cache Strategy
**Decision**: Hybrid approach (local cache → Nx Cloud)
- Start with local cache (M1-3) for simplicity
- Add Nx Cloud (M4) if performance requires
- Reduces upfront complexity

### AD-002: Package Structure
**Decision**: Preserve current `packages/` directory structure
- Minimizes migration complexity
- Maintains all import paths
- No breaking changes to consumers

### AD-003: Storybook Integration
**Decision**: Custom integration (wrap existing config)
- Keep working Storybook 10 configuration
- Wrap as Nx targets
- Lower migration risk

## 📊 Success Criteria

| Metric | Target | Rationale |
|--------|--------|-----------|
| Build Time | <110% baseline | No significant slowdown |
| Cache Hit Rate | >80% | Effective caching |
| CI Time | <80% baseline | 20%+ improvement |
| Test Pass Rate | 100% | No regressions |
| Developer Satisfaction | >80% | Team adoption |

## 🔄 Migration Approach

**Principles**:
- ✅ Incremental, milestone-based delivery
- ✅ Zero breaking changes to component APIs
- ✅ Each milestone independently deployable
- ✅ Comprehensive rollback procedures
- ✅ Preserve all existing tooling (Webpack, Babel, Gulp)

**Out of Scope** (for initial migration):
- ❌ Build tool replacement
- ❌ Test framework changes
- ❌ Package structure reorganization
- ❌ Component API changes

## 📚 References

This migration plan is based on the following resources and prior work:

### Internal Skyscanner Nx Migrations
- **banana Nx Migration**: https://skyscanner.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/UP1/pages/1353404332
  - Initial migration approach and lessons learned
- **banana Nx Follow-up**: https://skyscanner.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/UP1/pages/1362971958
  - Post-migration optimizations and refinements
- **falcon Nx Migration**: https://skyscanner.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/WOM/pages/1418986155
  - Alternative migration strategies and patterns
- **Backpack Nx Investigation**: https://skyscanner.atlassian.net/wiki/x/YAU9VQ
  - Initial feasibility study and technical analysis (note: may contain outdated information)

### Nx Ecosystem Documentation
- **Nx Official Documentation**: https://nx.dev/
  - Getting Started: https://nx.dev/getting-started/intro
  - Integrated Monorepo: https://nx.dev/concepts/integrated-vs-package-based
  - Caching: https://nx.dev/features/cache-task-results
  - CI/CD Integration: https://nx.dev/recipes/ci
  - Generators: https://nx.dev/plugin-features/use-code-generators
- **Nx Cloud**: https://nx.app/
  - Distributed caching and task execution

### Backpack-Specific References
- **Backpack Constitution**: `.specify/memory/constitution.md`
  - Core principles and non-negotiable standards
  - 13 principles including Modern Sass, Accessibility-First, TypeScript requirements
- **Architecture Decisions**: `decisions/` directory
  - 20+ decision documents covering naming, testing, styling, versioning
  - Key decisions: `modern-sass-api.md`, `sizing-in-rem.md`, `versioning-rules.md`
- **Backpack Repository**: https://github.com/Skyscanner/backpack

### Build Tools & Infrastructure

author: lazylemoncat
body:
## Summary
This PR implements stricter API return value handling in the PnL module to comply with the new development rules. Failed API calls now return `None` instead of default values (0.0, empty tuples, etc.), with proper validation and error handling throughout the call chain.

## Key Changes

- **Development Rules Documentation**: Added `CLAUDE.md` section defining language standards (Chinese for comments/responses) and API return value conventions (return `None` on failure, not default values)

- **Updated `_safe_float()` function**: 
  - Now accepts `Optional[float]` for default parameter
  - Returns `Optional[float]` instead of always returning a float
  - Allows callers to distinguish between valid zero values and failed conversions

- **Modified API price retrieval functions**:
  - `_get_deribit_current_price()`: Returns `None` on failure instead of `0.0`
  - `_get_pm_current_prices()`: Returns `(None, None)` on failure instead of `(0.0, 0.0)`
  - Added explicit null checks and logging for missing data in API responses

- **Enhanced `_calculate_position_pnl()` function**:
  - Now returns `Optional[PnlPositionDetail]` (can return `None`)
  - Added validation checks for all price sources (Deribit K1/K2, Polymarket, spot price)
  - Skips position calculation with warning logs when any required price is unavailable
  - Prevents silent failures from propagating invalid zero-value calculations

- **Improved `get_pnl_summary()` endpoint**:
  - Tracks skipped positions due to unavailable prices
  - Validates spot price before using it
  - Filters out `None` results from position detail calculations
  - Logs summary of skipped positions for monitoring

## Implementation Details

All price validation now follows a consistent pattern:
1. Retrieve raw value from API
2. Check for `None` explicitly
3. Convert to float with `_safe_float(..., default=None)`
4. Check result for `None` again
5. Return `None` or skip processing if validation fails

This ensures data integrity and makes pricing failures visible in logs rather than silently using zero values that could lead to incorrect PnL calculations.

author: danielclough
body:
# Add mimi encoder-only variant

- Add `EncoderOnly` struct to the mimi module that contains only encoder components (SeaNet encoder, transformer, downsampler, quantizer)
- Add `load_encoder_only()` convenience function for loading encoder-only weights
- Export new types from `mod.rs`

This enables loading Mimi encoder weights without requiring decoder weights, which is necessary for models like Qwen3-TTS that only distribute encoder weights for their speech tokenizer.

### Use Cases

- Qwen3-TTS speech tokenizer (encodes reference audio for voice cloning)
- Any audio model that needs encoding without decoding
- Reduced memory footprint when only encoding is needed

author: wi5nia
body:
## Summary

This PR migrates Azure KeyVault access control from the legacy access policy model to Azure RBAC, which is Microsoft's recommended approach for new deployments.

### Changes

- Enable `rbac_authorization_enabled` on the KeyVault resource
- Replace deployer access policy with `Key Vault Certificates Officer` role (least privilege for certificate management)
- Replace Application Gateway access policy with `Key Vault Secrets User` role (read-only access for SSL termination)
- Update certificate resource dependencies to use the new role assignments

### Why RBAC

- Unified access control model across Azure services
- Better security posture with separation of duties
- Integration with Privileged Identity Management (PIM)
- RBAC will become the default in Azure API version 2026-02-01

### Breaking Change

Existing deployments using access policies will need to either:
1. Recreate the KeyVault (recommended for clean state)
2. Manually migrate following [Microsoft's migration guide](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/key-vault/general/rbac-migration)

### Testing

Deployed and tested successfully in Sweden Central region with full infrastructure stack (AKS, PostgreSQL, Redis, Application Gateway).

Closes #26

author: mattsse
body:
## Summary

Adds a method to move precompiles from source addresses to destination addresses, supporting the `movePrecompileTo` field in `eth_simulateV1` state overrides.

## Changes

### New Error Type
- `MovePrecompileError` enum with `NotAPrecompile(Address)` variant
- Implements `Display`, `Debug`, `PartialEq`, `Eq`, `Clone`, and `Error`

### New Methods on `PrecompilesMap`
- `move_precompiles<I>(&mut self, moves: I) -> Result<(), MovePrecompileError>` - takes an iterator of `(source, dest)` pairs
- `with_moved_precompiles<I>(self, moves: I) -> Result<Self, MovePrecompileError>` - builder-style variant

### Behavior
- Validates all source addresses are precompiles before making any changes
- Skips moves where `source == dest` (no-op)
- Atomically removes from source and installs at destination
- Returns `NotAPrecompile` error if any source is not a precompile

## Example Usage

```rust
// Move ECRECOVER from 0x01 to a custom address
let moves = [(
    address!("0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000001"),
    address!("0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000100"),
)];
precompiles.move_precompiles(moves)?;
```

## Tests
- `test_move_precompiles` - basic move with verification
- `test_move_precompiles_not_a_precompile` - error case
- `test_move_precompiles_same_address_noop` - no-op case
- `test_move_precompiles_multiple` - moving multiple precompiles

author: aviatesk
body:
Add `copy_syntax_tree` function that creates lightweight copies of `SyntaxTree` objects by copying only the mutable structures (`edge_ranges`, `edges`, and attribute dictionaries) while sharing the immutable data within.

This is needed because JuliaLowering's pipeline modifies the internal `SyntaxGraph` structure. When multiple threads access the same cached tree (via `get_unsynced_file_info!`), this causes data races and segfaults. By returning a copy instead of the cached tree itself, each thread gets an independent tree to work with.

Also fix a TOCTOU race in `get_unsynced_file_info!` by moving the `haskey` check inside the `store!` callback, ensuring the check and update happen atomically.

Performance: `copy_syntax_tree` is ~100x faster than `build_tree` (~1μs vs ~100μs per file), so the caching optimization from aviatesk/JETLS.jl#505 is preserved.

author: copilot
body:
Implements fine-grained access control for data room documents and folders using email-based permissions, with comprehensive access tracking and blocking capabilities.

## Database Schema

Added 4 tables with indexed queries:
- `dataRoomEmailPermissions` - Permission rules (view/download/upload/manage) with folder/document allow/deny lists, IP restrictions, time windows, and download limits
- `dataRoomAccessAttempts` - Access logs with success/failure status and denial reasons
- `dataRoomEmailBlocks` - Email blocklist with optional auto-unblock timestamps
- `dataRoomPermissionAuditLog` - Permission change history

## Permission Enforcement

Added `checkEmailAccess()` with hierarchical precedence:
1. Email blocks → immediate denial
2. Denied folder/document IDs → override allowed lists
3. Email permissions → override invitation-based permissions
4. IP restrictions (allow/deny lists)
5. Download limits (atomic counter)
6. Time-based validity windows

```typescript
const accessCheck = await db.checkEmailAccess(dataRoomId, email, {
  documentId: 123,
  ipAddress: req.ip,
  action: 'download'
});

if (!accessCheck.hasAccess) {
  await db.logAccessAttempt({
    success: false,
    denialReason: accessCheck.reason,
    // ... metadata
  });
  throw new Error(accessCheck.reason);
}
```

## API Endpoints

- `dataRoom.emailPermissions.*` - CRUD for permission rules
- `dataRoom.accessAttempts.list` - Query access logs with filters
- `dataRoom.emailBlocks.*` - Manage blocked emails
- `dataRoom.auditLog.list` - Permission change history
- Enhanced `dataRoom.public.getContent` - Enforces permissions on folder/document filtering
- Enhanced `dataRoom.public.recordView` - Logs all access attempts

## Utilities

- `normalizeEmail()` - Consistent email normalization (trim + lowercase)
- `incrementDownloadCount()` - Atomic SQL increment to prevent race conditions

```typescript
// Prevents concurrent download race conditions
await db.incrementDownloadCount(permissionId);
// Uses: SET downloadCount = downloadCount + 1
```

body:
## ℹ️ Description

This PR addresses intermittent login detection failures that cause unnecessary re-logins and potential IP blocks.

- Link to the related issue(s): Issue #701
- **Motivation**: Users reported the bot sometimes fails to detect existing login sessions, especially after long inactivity (~20+ days). Unnecessary re-logins can trigger rate limiting and IP blocks.
- **Context**: PR #726 improved login detection with timeouts and better logging, but intermittent failures still occurred due to SPA hydration timing and DOM variability.

## 📋 Changes Summary

### Core Implementation
- **Server-side auth probe**: Added deterministic login state detection via `GET /m-meine-anzeigen-verwalten.json?sort=DEFAULT`
  - Probes first, falls back to DOM checks only when probe returns UNKNOWN
  - Eliminates false negatives from client-side rendering delays
- **LoginState enum**: Introduced `LOGGED_IN`, `LOGGED_OUT`, `UNKNOWN` states for explicit handling
- **Failure-only diagnostics**: Opt-in capture of screenshot + HTML when state is UNKNOWN
  - Config: `diagnostics.login_detection_capture` (default: false)
  - Safe default output directories based on installation mode
- **Interactive pause mode**: `diagnostics.pause_on_login_detection_failure` for manual browser inspection
  - Only activates in interactive terminals (TTY check)
  - Includes Pydantic validator to enforce dependency on capture being enabled

### Code Quality Improvements
- Defensive stdin check using `getattr(sys.stdin, "isatty", lambda: False)()`
- Updated log messages to reflect probe results
- Added German translations for new user-facing strings
- Comprehensive unit tests (151 new test lines)

### Documentation
- Updated `README.md` with login detection behavior explanation
- Enhanced `docs/BROWSER_TROUBLESHOOTING.md` with troubleshooting workflow
- Added PII warning for diagnostic artifacts
- Softened "deterministic" claims to acknowledge UNKNOWN fallback

**Configuration changes**:
```yaml
diagnostics:
  login_detection_capture: false  # Enable to capture artifacts on UNKNOWN
  pause_on_login_detection_failure: false  # Pause for manual inspection (interactive only)
  output_dir: null  # Optional custom output directory
```

**Dependencies**: None added

### Motivation
- Add automated Release Ops to bump package versions, create tags/releases, and notify on outcomes to reduce manual release work. 
- Tie deployments to Sentry releases so production errors are associated with the exact deploy. 
- Provide uniform Slack notifications for deploy success/failure across API, Genesis AI, and mobile flows for better team visibility.

### Description
- Add a new workflow `/.github/workflows/release.yml` that runs on `push` to `main` to compute a semver bump, update `package.json`, tag, and create a GitHub Release, and notify Slack on success/failure. 
- Add `scripts/release-version.js` (ESM) and a `release:version` npm script to compute the next semver using commit messages (`feat:` => minor, `fix:` => patch, `BREAKING CHANGE`/`!:` => major) and write the new version to `package.json`, callable via `node ./scripts/release-version.js`. 
- Update `package.json` to expose the `release:version` script. 
- Enhance deploy workflows with Sentry and Slack integration by adding a Sentry release step to API and Genesis AI deploys and adding Slack `success`/`failure` notification steps to `deploy-api.yml`, `deploy-ai.yml`, and `deploy-mobile.yml` that post to `secrets.SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL` using `jq` + `curl`.

### Testing
- No automated tests were executed as part of this change (these are CI/workflow additions and a local script); validation should be done by running the workflows in CI and by exercising the `release:version` script in a pipeline environment.

This PR implements the /pallets/foreign-assets endpoint to retrieve all foreign assets (cross-chain assets identified by XCM MultiLocation) from Asset Hub chains, with full support for historical block queries.

1. Changes Made
**Foreign Assets Endpoint**
Added foreign_assets.rs handler implementing:
- GET /v1/pallets/foreign-assets - Returns all foreign assets with their MultiLocation, asset info, and metadata

2. Implementation Details
- Uses dynamic storage queries with subxt to fetch ForeignAssets::Asset and ForeignAssets::Metadata
- Correctly queries historical state when using ?at= parameter
- Custom SCALE decoding for XCM MultiLocation with proper handling of:
- Compact<u64> for Ethereum chainId
- Compact<u32> for Parachain numbers
- Compact<u128> for GeneralIndex
- Pre-fetches all metadata entries using blake2_128_concat key matching for efficient lookups
- Converts account IDs to SS58 format matching the chain's prefix
- Supports useRcBlock for Asset Hub chains (relay chain block queries)
- RC block handler iterates ALL Asset Hub blocks in a relay chain block and returns an array

3. Query Parameters
- at (optional): Block height or hash. Defaults to finalized block if not provided
- useRcBlock (optional): Use relay chain block reference (Asset Hub only)

4. Route Configuration
Updated routes with:
- /pallets/foreign-assets → pallets::foreign_assets::pallets_foreign_assets

5. Response Format
- multiLocation - XCM location with camelCase field names
- foreignAssetInfo - Owner, issuer, admin, freezer (SS58), supply, deposit, minBalance, accounts, sufficients, approvals, status
- foreignAssetMetadata - Name, symbol, decimals, deposit

body:
This pull request introduces significant enhancements to the code compactor functionality, focusing on semantic understanding of code structures and improved pattern recognition. The implementation now includes a new SemanticCompactor class that replaces previous brace-based approaches with more intelligent code collapsing capabilities.

Key improvements include:

- Enhanced pattern recognition for imports, test blocks, functions, and object literals
- Brace matching functionality for nested structures
- Single-line logical unit detection to prevent unnecessary collapsing
- Performance optimizations including early exit for small files
- Comprehensive test coverage for all new functionality

The changes also address previous limitations in recognizing and preserving code structures that should remain intact during compaction, such as import statements, test blocks with object literals, and class declarations.

author: werb210
body:
### Motivation
- Stop runtime crashes and navigation errors by hardening auth flows, routing, and settings UI so pages never render with undefined/partial data. 
- Add Microsoft 365 sign-in support (non-blocking) alongside OTP without introducing binary assets. 
- Make lenders/products and settings pages null-safe to prevent fatal renders during navigation or missing data. 

### Description
- Login: added Microsoft 365 (MSAL) login handling with redirect/popup handling, exchange endpoint call, UI states for loading/errors, a non-binary “Continue with Microsoft 365” button, and inputs disabling while verifying; preserved text-only behavior and guarded undefined auth state (`src/pages/login/LoginPage.tsx`, `src/styles/globals.css`).
- Routing & Settings: introduced settings overview and `/settings/:tab` routing, wired sidebar link for Settings, and navigational guards so tab changes resolve to stable pages instead of crashing (`src/pages/settings/SettingsPage.tsx`, `src/router/index.tsx`, `src/components/layout/Sidebar.tsx`, `src/App.tsx`).
- Route guards: tightened `PrivateRoute`, `ProtectedRoute`, and `RequireAuth` to wait for roles/user readiness and render safe loading skeletons instead of letting pages mount with incomplete auth (`src/router/PrivateRoute.tsx`, `src/routes/ProtectedRoute.tsx`, `src/routes/RequireAuth.tsx`).
- Lenders & Products: added null-safe fallbacks for lender/product names, categories, amounts and currency fields to avoid unexpected exceptions when data is missing (`src/pages/lenders/LendersPage.tsx`).
- PWA & SW: stop caching or referencing binary icons in the service worker and limit cached assets to text-like entries; add a small `getDisplayMode` utility and propagate display-mode to `document` for safer iPad/PWA logic (`src/sw.ts`, `src/utils/pwa.ts`, `src/App.tsx`).
- Tests & test infra: added a smoke test suite that asserts core pages render and that no runtime errors are logged, and added a lightweight test alias/mock for `@azure/msal-browser` so tests run without installing browser-only MSAL code (`src/tests/app.smoke.test.tsx`, `src/test/msalBrowserMock.ts`, `vite.config.ts`, `src/test/setupTests.ts`).
- Minor: small UI CSS for the login divider/button and other defensive cleanups; removed service worker references to icon files (no binary changes added).

### Testing

body: fixes #461 ## 📋 Overview This PR introduces a sophisticated reporting layer to the SoulSense Assessment tool. The goal was to transform raw numerical scores into **actionable emotional insights** that users can keep and review. I have also cleaned up the repository by properly untracking autogenerated database files and environment artifacts to ensure a professional codebase. --- ## ✨ Key Features ### 1. Temporal Sentiment Velocity Engine (`app/analytics.py`) Instead of just tracking 1-5 scores, I integrated **Natural Language Processing (NLP)** via `TextBlob`. * **The Logic:** It analyzes the "Stressor" text input provided by the user at the start of the quiz. * **The Benefit:** It calculates the "Polarity" (emotional weight) to categorize the user's current state (e.g., "Coping Well" vs. "High Stress"). ### 2. Professional PDF Reporting Engine (`app/report_engine.py`) I added a dedicated report generator using the `fpdf` library. * **User Control:** The report is **not** forced on the user. After the quiz, a custom UI popup appears, allowing the user to choose to download the report. * **Portability:** This turns session data into a professional document that can be saved locally. ### 3. Repository Hygiene * **`.gitignore` Fixes:** I've updated the ignore rules and used `git rm --cached` to ensure that `soulsense_db.db` and `__pycache__` are no longer tracked. --- it is automatically calculated but manually saved. --- ## 🛠️ Technical Implementation Details * **New Dependencies:** `textblob`, `fpdf` * **Architecture Changes:** * `app/analytics.py`: Custom module for NLP sentiment calculation. * `app/report_engine.py`: Logic for PDF formatting and file generation. * `app/__init__.py`: Standardized the directory as a Python package for clean imports. * `app.py`: Integrated the new lifecycle flow (Quiz -> Analysis -> Download -> Exit). ## 🧪 Testing Performed - [x] **NLP Validation:** Verified sentiment polarity correctly identifies "Positive" vs "Stressed" strings. - [x] **UI Lifecycle:** Confirmed the `Download` button triggers the file save and then closes the app safely. - [x] **Environment:** Verified that the local database file is now correctly ignored by Git. ---

author: copilot
body:
Enables programmatic playback control and minimal UI mode. Previously, controls were always rendered and could only be controlled through internal UI.

## Changes

- **Ref forwarding**: Exposes `play()`, `pause()`, `seek(time)`, and `resumeAudioContext()` methods via `WaveformNavigatorHandle`
- **showControls prop**: Boolean (default `true`) to conditionally render built-in controls
- **Type exports**: Added `WaveformNavigatorHandle` interface for TypeScript consumers

## Usage

### Programmatic control with custom UI

```tsx
import { useRef } from 'react';
import WaveformNavigator, { WaveformNavigatorHandle } from 'waveform-navigator';

function App() {
  const waveformRef = useRef<WaveformNavigatorHandle>(null);
  
  const handlePlay = async () => {
    await waveformRef.current?.resumeAudioContext(); // Safari/iOS requirement
    await waveformRef.current?.play();
  };
  
  return (
    <>
      <WaveformNavigator 
        ref={waveformRef}
        audio="/audio.mp3"
        showControls={false}
      />
      <button onClick={handlePlay}>Play</button>
      <button onClick={() => waveformRef.current?.pause()}>Pause</button>
      <button onClick={() => waveformRef.current?.seek(30)}>Skip to 30s</button>
    </>
  );
}
```

### Minimal waveform-only display

```tsx
<WaveformNavigator 
  audio="/audio.mp3"
  showControls={false}
  height={60}
/>
```

## Demo

**Default mode with built-in controls:**
![With controls](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2b695bc1-cd35-4c28-a47b-880788cbde17)

**Minimal UI with programmatic control:**
![Without controls](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2ced7690-37a3-4f90-8d48-ab138d5c65c8)

## Implementation Notes

- `play()` includes error handling for DOMException with contextual messages
- `resumeAudioContext()` creates temporary AudioContext to enable audio on Safari/iOS
- Zero breaking changes: all existing functionality preserved
- Added 6 unit tests (29 total passing)

body:
Problem: Loading Django URL patterns triggered a cascade of imports that eventually hit a buggy Evennia module (evmenu.py), causing goals and conditions APIs to fail with TypeError.

Import chain:
views.py → typeclasses.characters → commands.utils → commands.__init__ → commands.evennia_overrides.builder → evennia.commands.default.building → evennia.prototypes.menus → evennia.utils.evmenu (bug)

Solution:
- Use TYPE_CHECKING guards in goals/views.py and conditions/views.py for Character type hints (runtime doesn't need the import)
- Remove module-level command imports from commands/__init__.py, commands/account/__init__.py, and commands/evennia_overrides/__init__.py
- Add CI test suite to prevent regression

The test suite verifies:
- URL loading doesn't import evennia.commands.default.building
- goals.urls and conditions.urls don't import typeclasses.characters
- commands/__init__.py doesn't import command classes

author: akash-m-se
body:
### Description

This pull request introduces a comprehensive **Credential Management System**, significantly enhances the user interface for entity display, and refactors the API for improved scalability and maintainability. The core of this update is to allow users to securely store, manage, and utilize credentials for third-party services within their workflows.

### Key Changes

#### Features:

*   **Secure Credential Management:**
    *   **Full CRUD Functionality:** Users can now create, view, update, and delete credentials through a new set of dedicated pages and components.
    *   **Database Integration:** A new `Credential` model has been added to the database schema to securely store encrypted credential data, associated with a user.
    *   **AI Provider Integration:** The Anthropic, Gemini, and OpenAI integrations have been updated to use the new credential management system, allowing users to select a credential from a dropdown instead of relying on environment variables.
    *   **Workflow Integration:** The `Node` model has been updated to allow individual nodes within a workflow to be configured to use specific credentials.

*   **UI/UX Enhancements:**
    *   **Improved Entity Layout:** The `EntityItem` component, used on the "Workflows" and "Credentials" pages, has been refactored for a cleaner, more responsive, and more organized card-based layout.
    *   **Responsive Design:** The layout of entity cards is now responsive, ensuring a great user experience on both desktop and mobile devices.

#### Refactoring and Code Quality:

*   **Generic API Responses:** A new generic `PaginatedResponse<T>` type has been introduced to standardize the structure of all paginated API responses, improving consistency and reducing code duplication.
*   **Centralized Input Validation:** A common schema for pagination and search parameters has been created and implemented, centralizing validation logic and ensuring consistency across API endpoints.
*   **Updated Services and Hooks:** The services and hooks related to workflows have been updated to align with the new generic pagination types, improving type safety and simplifying the data flow.

#### Bug Fixes:

*   **Credential Fetching:** Fixed a bug where the `fetchCredentialByType` function in the credentials router was not returning any value.

author: jonahgabriel
body:
## Summary

Refactor all omnimemory handlers to follow the canonical `omnibase_infra` container-driven pattern established by `HandlerGraph` (OMN-1515).

- Migrate 7 handlers to container-driven pattern with `ModelONEXContainer` as single constructor parameter
- Add `initialize()`, `health_check()`, and `describe()` methods to all handlers
- Handler now owns adapter/dependency lifecycle (creates on init, closes on shutdown)
- Update all call sites (registries, tests, docstrings)

## Handlers Refactored

| Handler | Location | Priority |
|---------|----------|----------|
| `HandlerIntentQuery` | `nodes/intent_query_effect/handlers/` | High |
| `HandlerSemanticCompute` | `handlers/handler_semantic_compute.py` | Medium |
| `HandlerSubscription` | `handlers/handler_subscription.py` | Medium |
| `HandlerMemoryExpire` | `nodes/memory_lifecycle_orchestrator/handlers/` | Low |
| `HandlerMemoryTick` | `nodes/memory_lifecycle_orchestrator/handlers/` | Low |
| `HandlerMemoryArchive` | `nodes/memory_lifecycle_orchestrator/handlers/` | Low |
| `HandlerSimilarityCompute` | `nodes/similarity_compute/handlers/` | Low |

## Pattern Applied

**Before (inconsistent)**:
```python
class HandlerFoo:
    def __init__(self, config: Config, adapter: Adapter) -> None:
        self._config = config
        self._adapter = adapter  # lifecycle ownership unclear
```

**After (container-driven)**:
```python
class HandlerFoo:
    def __init__(self, container: ModelONEXContainer) -> None:
        self._container = container
        self._adapter: Adapter | None = None
        self._initialized = False

    async def initialize(self, connection_uri: str, **opts) -> None:
        self._adapter = Adapter(...)  # handler owns lifecycle
        await self._adapter.initialize(...)
        self._initialized = True

    async def health_check(self) -> dict: ...
    async def describe(self) -> dict: ...
```

## Test plan

- [x] All handler unit tests pass (288 passed)
- [x] Pre-commit hooks pass (ruff, mypy, custom validators)
- [x] New tests added for `health_check()` and `describe()` methods
- [ ] CI pipeline validation

## Related

- Closes OMN-1577
- Related: OMN-1515 (HandlerGraph pattern reference)
- Related: OMN-1536 (HandlerIntent - uses correct pattern from start)

### Summary
Changes to recipe:  **at-spi2-core/2.59.0**

#### Motivation

When building GTK-3, the requirements atk and atk-bridge are needed. However, the glib version will result in conflict due to the version ranges. This PR not only solves the glib conflict, but also adds the latest version and stops publishing new revisions for old versions.

#### Details
