## Summary
This PR enhances site performance, search engine optimization, and accessibility by implementing aggressive caching headers, standardizing Open Graph and Twitter metadata across pages, improving focus states for keyboard navigation, and removing unused backup files.

## Key Changes

**Performance & Caching**
- Added cache headers to `_headers` for static assets:
  - Images, JS, and CSS: 1-year immutable cache (max-age=31536000)
  - Data files: 1-hour cache (max-age=3600)

**SEO & Social Media**
- Added `og:type="website"` meta tag to all pages (index, about, calculator, contact, faq, resources, services)
- Added `twitter:image` meta tag pointing to WebP version of og-hero image across all pages
- Improves social media preview consistency and image optimization

**Accessibility**
- Updated focus styles from `:focus` to `:focus-visible` for better keyboard navigation UX
- Added focus outlines to:
  - `.cta` button (2px solid outline with offset)
  - `.btn-primary` and `.cta-button` (2px solid outline with offset)
  - `.res-chip` filter buttons (2px solid outline with offset)
  - `.floating-state-btn` (2px solid white outline with offset)
- Ensures visible focus indicators only appear for keyboard users, not mouse users

**Code Cleanup**
- Removed backup/unused files:
  - `articles/flexible-parking-rules/index.backup.html`
  - `css/article.backup.css`
  - `images/rules.jpg`
  - `metadata-audit.xlsx`
  - `metadata-recommendations.xlsx`
- Removed unused `submitForm()` function from `script.js`
- Added safety check for `gtag` function existence before calling analytics events

## Implementation Details
- Focus styles now use `outline-offset: 2px` for better visual separation
- Analytics event tracking now guards against undefined `gtag` to prevent runtime errors
- Cache headers follow best practices: immutable assets get long TTL, dynamic data gets shorter TTL

body:
### Motivation
- Add a basic subscriptions flow (Stripe checkout + webhook) so users can upgrade tariffs and have limits applied automatically. 
- Enforce tariff-based limits to prevent users on lower plans from running campaigns that exceed their account allowance. 
- Improve frontend UX for MVP readiness with subscription UI, nicer error pages, loading skeletons and Telegram WebApp MainButton integration. 
- Prepare CI/deployment and dev docs for load testing and production deploys. 

### Description
- Wire Stripe keys into settings and `.env.example`, add `stripe` dependency, implement `POST /admin/subscriptions/create-checkout` in admin API to create checkout sessions, and add `/webhook/stripe` in the backend to handle `checkout.session.completed` metadata and update `user.tariff_id`. 
- Enforce tariff account limits in campaign startup by checking `current_user.tariff.max_accounts` against actual account count and returning `400` when exceeded, while preserving existing daily-invite rate checks. 
- Add frontend `Subscription` page and navigation link, wire `createAdminCheckoutSession` to call the admin checkout endpoint and redirect users to Stripe, and document Stripe env variables in `README.md`. 
- UX polish: add `ErrorPage` (403/429/500), `SkeletonList` and `EmptyState` components, integrate Telegram `WebApp.MainButton` handlers on Campaigns and Accounts pages to surface key actions, and add many frontend pages/containers and styles for the MVP UI. 
- Platform and infra additions: add Prometheus/Grafana/blackbox/3proxy config and Docker Compose manifests, a backend Dockerfile, Alembic migrations and ORM models/schemas, core services (limits, rate limiting, websocket manager, proxy sync/validation), Celery workers and tasks, and GitHub Actions workflows to run tests/builds and a release deploy placeholder. 
- API and client plumbing: expanded `resources` client, new admin endpoints for tariffs/users/proxies/accounts, auth flow, and many server-side schemas, tests and helper utilities. 

### Testing
- No automated tests were executed in this environment; a GitHub Actions CI job was added that installs dependencies, runs `pytest backend/tests`, compiles the backend and builds the frontend (`cd frontend && npm run build`). 
- A comprehensive unit/integration test suite was added under `backend/tests/` to cover accounts, campaigns, tariffs, limits, proxy validation, websockets and workers, but these tests were not run locally here. 
- Basic runtime readiness endpoints were left in place for manual smoke checks (`GET /health` and `GET /metrics`) and will be exercised by CI/deploy pipelines. 
- Documentation updated with Stripe env vars and a load-testing note (`locust -f locustfile.py --users 100`) to guide stress testing prior to production.

- `test_route_prefix_basic_endpoints` - Health and catalog endpoints under prefix
- `test_route_prefix_tile_endpoints` - TileJSON and tile data under prefix
- `test_base_path_overrides_route_prefix` - Priority behavior
- `test_nested_route_prefix` - Deep nesting support
- `test_route_prefix_root_path` - Root path normalization

### Implementation Details

**Configuration:**
- `route_prefix`: Affects actual API routing - **all endpoints** (including metrics) served under this path
- `base_path`: Only affects TileJSON URL generation (existing behavior unchanged)
- Priority for TileJSON URLs: `base_path` > `route_prefix` > `x-rewrite-url` > request path
- Special case: `route_prefix: "/"` is normalized to no prefix (None)

**Routing:**
- When `route_prefix` is set, all routes are wrapped in `web::scope(prefix)`
- **Metrics endpoint (`/_/metrics`) also respects the route_prefix** - becomes `{route_prefix}/_/metrics`
- Refactored to use a standalone function instead of closure for better readability
- Maintains all existing middleware and feature flags

**Documentation:**
- Updated docs/src/config.yaml with clear explanation of both options
- Explains the difference and priority between route_prefix and base_path

**Testing:**
- Consolidated tests to eliminate duplication
- Each test now covers multiple related endpoints
- Maintains full test coverage with fewer, more focused tests

This PR changes the "naive" test+hazard+benchmark to use the new 1.0 naive prompts.

The naive prompts are 10% of the general holdback set. This subset isn’t being used anywhere else, so we created a new file which I added to `SECURITY_NAIVE_PROMPT_SETS`.

Important note: security benchmarks are now meaningless because we don't have 1.0 attack prompts yet. So if you were to run a security benchmark, it would run 1.0 naive prompts and 0.5 jailbreaks. I changed the version of the benchmark to "0.0" in case someone were to run it (either via baas or one of us runs it accidentally), but maybe we should disable the security benchmark cli entirely?

#### Description
Sometimes collecting docker stats would fail with `"error": "context canceled"`

It's because it was cancelling the context concurrently with reading the response. If reading the response takes a little bit of time it would cancel instead of reading the response.

Move context and cancellation outside to the calling function so that it can do parsing before cancelling the timeout.

#### Link to tracking issue
Fixes #34194
https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/34320
https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-demo/issues/1677

#### Testing
Added a reproduction integration test that simulates a slightly slow response.

body:
Due to my work stuff, I was trying to use IcedTea-Web browser plugin in firefox browser on Debian 12 to run some java applets.
When I built this plugin from source, the plugin was crashing as it tried to initialize. After some debugging, I found out that the plugin was crashing when it encountered null bytes in a UTF-8 encoded stream.
I think it was attempting to read from the appletviewer channel to check whether the JVM was running. Due to changes in the version of Glib used in Debian 12, the library no longer accepted null bytes in UTF-8 streams, which caused the plugin to crash when such bytes were present. At least that's what I understood from the research I did.

This update changes the encoding to NULL so it accepts all data.

I know this is legacy and probably only a handful of people still use the browser plugin, but I figured I’d share it in case someone wants to use it like I have to

## Summary

Implements graph-to-grid-graph mapping using the copy-line technique from UnitDiskMapping.jl, enabling reductions to unit disk graphs on both square and triangular lattices.

- Add `GridGraph` type for weighted graphs on 2D integer lattices (square and triangular)
- Add copy-line embedding infrastructure for mapping arbitrary graph vertices
- Add gadget system with 9 square-lattice gadgets and 3 triangular-lattice gadgets
- Add `map_graph()` and `map_graph_triangular()` functions for complete graph mapping
- Add `MappingResult` with solution back-mapping via `map_config_back()`
- Add 37 integration tests covering various graph types

- [x] Integration tests cover path, triangle, star, K4, empty, and disconnected graphs
- [x] Serialization tests verify `MappingResult` round-trips correctly
- [x] Both square and triangular lattice mappings tested

body:
### Motivation
- Evitar envíos dobles y mejorar la experiencia de usuario durante la importación de archivos CSV en el panel de administración. 
- Añadir un indicador visual y bloqueo de controles mientras hay una request en curso para las subidas de diccionarios y maestro. 
- Seguir el plan de crear una rama de feature y validar la build del frontend antes de proponer el PR.

### Description
- Se actualizó `src/pages/Admin.jsx` para agregar dos flags de estado `isUploadingDic` y `isUploadingMae` y un derived flag `isUploading` para representar cargas en curso. 
- Las funciones de subida por archivo (`importarDicPorArchivo` e `importarMaePorArchivo`) ahora previenen reentradas, establecen los flags adecuados y limpian el estado en `finally`. 
- Se deshabilitan los campos `type="file"` y los botones de envío mientras `isUploading` es true y se añadió un `Spinner` y texto `Cargando…` como indicador visible. 

### Testing
- Ejecuté `npm run build` y la construcción de Vite finalizó correctamente sin errores. 
- Arranqué el servidor de desarrollo con `npm run dev` y realicé una comprobación automatizada headless (Playwright) que capturó una captura de pantalla de la sección de importación para verificar visualmente los controles. 
- Se creó un commit con el mensaje `Add upload loading state for admin imports` en la rama `feature/upload-loading-state`.```

body:
## Summary

- Add `txray decode <calldata>` command for decoding transaction input data
- Support fetching calldata from transaction with `--tx <hash>` flag
- Recursive decoding for nested calls (e.g., multicall patterns)

## Features

### Calldata Decoding
- Uses loaded ABIs from `abi/` folder for decoding
- Falls back to selector lookup when ABI unavailable
- Shows function name, selector, and decoded parameters

### Nested Call Detection
- Automatically detects and decodes nested call patterns
- Handles arrays of calls (common in multicall/batch transactions)
- Visual tree output for complex calldata

### Transaction Lookup
- `--tx <hash>` flag fetches calldata from transaction
- `--chain <id>` specifies chain for lookup (default: 1)

## Usage

```bash
# Decode raw calldata
txray decode 0xa9059cbb000000000000...

# Decode from transaction
txray decode --tx 0xabc123... --chain 1

# With custom labels
txray decode 0xa9059cbb... --labels ./my-labels.json
```

## Files Changed

- `src/decode.ts` - New module for calldata decoding
- `src/cli.ts` - Added `decode` subcommand

Implements Phase 1, PR #4 from PLAN.md

author: justinh-rahb
body:
### Added
- **File Access**:
  - Added dedicated "Files" button to the Global Header for quick access from any screen.
  - File Browser can now be opened during active prints (view-only), allowing file management and inspection without interrupting the job.
- **File Management**:
  - Full file capabilities in File Browser: Delete (files & directories), Rename, Move, and Create New Folder.
  - Double-click to enter directories, single-click to select for actions.
- **UI Improvements**:
  - **Tabbed Settings**: Settings Modal now organized into 5 logical tabs (General, Interface, Macros, Panels, Cameras) to reduce scrolling and improve navigability.
  - **Modal Scroll Lock**: Background page scrolling is now locked when any modal is open (Settings, Connection, File Picker, Confirmation dialogs).
- Temperature Panel improvements
  - **Autoscale Graph**: Graph Y-axis now dynamically scales to the highest visible temperature (plus 10% buffer), improving visibility for lower-temp prints (e.g., PLA at 200°C vs 300°C max).
  - **Interactive Cursor**: Hovering over the graph now displays a vertical cursor and a floating tooltip showing exact temperature values for all sensors at that specific time point.
  - **Hide Monitors**: New setting to hide passive temperature sensors (like Raspberry Pi or MCU temps) from the graph and list, focusing only on heaters (Bed, Extruder).
  - **Hide Graph**: Option to completely hide the temperature graph for a compact view.
  - **Settings Integration**: New "TEMPERATURE DISPLAY" section in Settings Modal to toggle these features. Preserves user preferences.

### Changed
- **Settings UX**: 
  - Relocated "Save" button in Settings Modal to the header bar for quicker access.
  - Updated "Save" button style to match other action buttons (orange gradient).
  - Standardized "Close" button style across Settings and File Picker modals.
- **File Browser UX**: 
  - Relocated "Upload" button to the header for consistency.
  - Reorganized footer actions to accommodate new file management tools in a clearer layout.
- **Visuals**:
  - Improved modal positioning: Settings and File Picker modals now have a fixed top offset to prevent vertical jumping during content resizing.
  - Consistent modal width for Settings and File Picker.

### Fixed
- Speed Factor and Extrusion Factor sliders now properly sync with the printer
  - Sliders now send M220 (speed) and M221 (extrusion) G-code commands when changed
  - Previously, slider changes only updated local UI state and were immediately overwritten by subscription updates from Moonraker

body:
## Summary

Audited all Repository implementations for N+1 query issues. Found and fixed inefficient query patterns in `LikeRepository.FindLikedArticlesByUserAsync` and removed unnecessary eager loading in `CommentRepository.FindByIdAsync`.

## Changes

### LikeRepository.FindLikedArticlesByUserAsync

Consolidated two-query pattern with in-memory join into single optimized query:

**Before:**
```csharp
// Query 1: Fetch like metadata
var likedArticles = await context.Likes
    .Select(l => new { l.ArticleId, l.CreatedAt })
    .ToListAsync();

// Query 2: Fetch articles separately
var articles = await context.Articles
    .Where(a => articleIds.Contains(a.Id))
    .Include(...)
    .ToListAsync();

// Memory join to preserve order
var orderedArticles = likedArticles
    .Select(la => articles.FirstOrDefault(a => a.Id == la.ArticleId))
    .ToList();
```

**After:**
```csharp
var articles = await context.Likes
    .Where(l => l.UserId == userId)
    .Where(l => l.Article != null)
    .Include(l => l.Article).ThenInclude(a => a.Author)
    .Include(l => l.Article.ArticleTags).ThenInclude(at => at.Tag)
    .Include(l => l.Article.Likes)
    .OrderByDescending(l => l.CreatedAt)
    .AsSplitQuery()
    .Select(l => l.Article)
    .ToListAsync();
```

Uses `AsSplitQuery()` to avoid cartesian explosion with multiple includes while maintaining sort order.

### CommentRepository.FindByIdAsync

Removed unused `Article` navigation property include. Method is currently unused and doesn't require full article data.

```diff
  return await context.Comments
      .Include(c => c.User)
-     .Include(c => c.Article)
      .FirstOrDefaultAsync(c => c.Id == id);
```

## Audit Results

All other repositories verified to use proper eager loading:
- ArticleRepository: Consistent use of `.Include()` across all methods
- FollowRepository: Uses `.Select()` for navigation properties
- UserRepository: No navigation property usage

body:
This pull request fixes a bug where the action summary incorrectly showed "Would update X (PR #N)" for PRs that were already up-to-date, even though the logs correctly showed "PR #N already has the latest". The fix improves visibility by showing existing PRs that are pending merge.

## Problem

When a PR exists with content that matches the source, the logs correctly showed:
```
✓ PR #84 already has the latest dependabot.yml
```

But the summary incorrectly showed:
```
Would update dependabot.yml (PR #84)
```

This was confusing because there was nothing to update.

## Solution

- **Fixed `getChangesList`**: Add explicit handling for `pr-up-to-date` status across all 8 sync types (dependabot.yml, .gitignore, rulesets, PR templates, workflow files, autolinks, copilot instructions, package.json)
- **Updated summary display**: Now shows informative "pending merge" message: `dependabot.yml PR #84 up-to-date (pending merge)`
- **Fixed `hasRepositoryChanges`**: Treat `pr-up-to-date` as a reportable status (not hidden like `unchanged`), so users can see which repos have pending PRs

## Before vs After

| Before | After |
|--------|-------|
| Would update dependabot.yml (PR #84) | dependabot.yml PR #84 up-to-date (pending merge) |
| (misleading - nothing to update) | (clear - PR exists and is ready to merge) |

## Changes

### Bug fixes
- Fixed `pr-up-to-date` status falling through to incorrect else branch in `getChangesList`
- Corrected summary output to match actual state

### Improvements  
- Added `hasSyncChanges` helper function to centralize change detection logic
- PRs pending merge are now visible in summary (previously hidden)

### Tests
- Added 3 new tests for `pr-up-to-date` summary handling
- Tests verify pending merge messages display correctly for dependabot and workflow files
- Tests verify `pr-up-to-date` is treated as a reportable change

The commit above lacks any documentation but GitHub associates the pull request (159).
The pull request (159) associates the referenced issue (145).
The issue (145) appears to not relate to the actual changes made.
Instead, the correct pull request is likely 184 with associated issue 177.

The only description provided is in the issue title: "Correct person's academic article publication outlet ampersand encoding".

However, to favor security practices, I have opted to use the default.

body:
# PR Title: Fix/Recover from "Jan 26 Crisis" (Stability, Logging, Cleanup)

## 📌 Summary
This PR resolves the critical instability issues ("vanishing logs," "broken search") introduced by recent merges. It effectively "unbricks" the application by decoupling frontend/backend logic and hardening the startup process. Additionally, it performs a major cleanup of the repository structure to address team feedback.

## 💥 The Problem (Why this is needed)
*   **Circular Dependency:** `frontend` and `backend` locked each other up during import.
*   **Logging Hijack:** The backend was resetting logging configuration, making debug logs invisible.
*   **Fragile Imports:** Opening a python file without valid API keys would crash the app immediately.
*   **Cluttered Repo:** Root directory was full of test scripts and doc files.

## 🛠️ Key Changes

### 1. Stability & Architecture 🏗️
*   **Decoupled Logic:** Created [backend/filters.py](cci:7://file:///Users/daai6ga1hou2/Documents/GitHub/VentureCapital/adk-grant-seeker-copilot/backend/filters.py:0:0-0:0) to host shared logic ([apply_filters_to_results](cci:1://file:///Users/daai6ga1hou2/Documents/GitHub/VentureCapital/adk-grant-seeker-copilot/frontend/search_grants.py:332:0-423:19)), breaking the circular dependency between [adk_agent.py](cci:7://file:///Users/daai6ga1hou2/Documents/GitHub/VentureCapital/adk-grant-seeker-copilot/backend/adk_agent.py:0:0-0:0) and [search_grants.py](cci:7://file:///Users/daai6ga1hou2/Documents/GitHub/VentureCapital/adk-grant-seeker-copilot/frontend/search_grants.py:0:0-0:0).
*   **Safe Runtime Init:** Moved API Key validation and Google Client initialization from **Module Level** (import time) to **[__init__](cci:1://file:///Users/daai6ga1hou2/Documents/GitHub/VentureCapital/adk-grant-seeker-copilot/backend/google_search_client.py:13:4-23:9)** (runtime). This prevents import-time crashes.
*   **Restored Logging:** Removed global `logging.basicConfig` from [adk_agent.py](cci:7://file:///Users/daai6ga1hou2/Documents/GitHub/VentureCapital/adk-grant-seeker-copilot/backend/adk_agent.py:0:0-0:0). The app is now responsible for logging configuration, restoring visibility.
*   **Syntax Fixes:** Fixed duplicate `except` blocks and indentation errors in [tavily_client.py](cci:7://file:///Users/daai6ga1hou2/Documents/GitHub/VentureCapital/adk-grant-seeker-copilot/backend/tavily_client.py:0:0-0:0), [google_search_client.py](cci:7://file:///Users/daai6ga1hou2/Documents/GitHub/VentureCapital/adk-grant-seeker-copilot/backend/google_search_client.py:0:0-0:0), and [adk_agent.py](cci:7://file:///Users/daai6ga1hou2/Documents/GitHub/VentureCapital/adk-grant-seeker-copilot/backend/adk_agent.py:0:0-0:0).

### 2. Repository Cleanup 🧹
*   **Organized Folders:**
    *   Moved `test_*.py` -> `tests/`
    *   Moved `*_PLAN.md`, `*_GUIDE.md` -> `docs/`
    *   Moved utility scripts -> `scripts/`
*   **Docs Update:** Updated [README.md](cci:7://file:///Users/daai6ga1hou2/Documents/GitHub/VentureCapital/adk-grant-seeker-copilot/README.md:0:0-0:0) to reflect the new structure and addressed team feedback (removed specific test counts).

## ✅ Verification
I have verified these changes with a new test script ([verify_fix.py](cci:7://file:///Users/daai6ga1hou2/Documents/GitHub/VentureCapital/adk-grant-seeker-copilot/scripts/verify_fix.py:0:0-0:0) - run locally) and the existing test suite:
*   `tests/test_filters.py`: **PASSED** (Proves search > extract > filter loop works)
*   `tests/test_iterative_search.py`: **PASSED** (Proves API connectivity)
*   Manual Check: Logs are now visible in the console/Streamlit output.

body: ## Description A number of the content items in the "Tasks - All" collection of the CMS have information that pertains to state licenses. This information may be useful to our end users of the static site. This work enables specified items within this collection to be synced with Webflow. ### Ticket This pull request resolves [#17102](https://dev.azure.com/NJInnovation/Business%20First%20Stop/_workitems/edit/17102). ### Approach - Updated the collection "Tasks - All" so that items can have an optional "Sync to Webflow" property - Updated `licenseLoader.mjs` to load `.md` files from the "Tasks - All" collection _**if**_ they should be`syncToWebflow` - The `licensesSync.mjs` file will create new or modify existing license records in the Webflow CMS with these tasks included. **Update to Decap CMS Collection "Tasks - All"** **Post licenses sync - Content in Webflow CMS** **Content modified with new webflow id** ### Steps to Test - Create a new or modify an existing content item in "Tasks - All" so that `syncToWebflow` is `true` - Run the `licensesSync.mjs` script - A new record should be created in the Webflow CMS within the Licenses collection, and the item you modified should have a `webflowId` associated with it - Tasks where `syncToWebflow` is not `true` should not be synced ### Notes "Tasks - All" is very close, but not an exact match to "License Tasks" (the collection being sync'd to Webflow today). body:
## Summary

- Adds new `forward` command for SSH port forwarding to view servers running on remote instances
- Opens SSH tunnel with `-L` port forwarding and automatically opens browser
- Supports port specification as `8000` (same local/remote) or `8000:3000` (local:remote)

## Usage

```bash
# Forward port 8000 on default instance to localhost:8000
remote instance forward 8000

# Forward remote port 3000 to local port 8000
remote instance forward 8000:3000

# Forward from specific instance
remote instance forward 8000 my-server

# Don't automatically open browser
remote instance forward 8000 --no-browser

# Auto-start instance if stopped
remote instance forward 8000 --start
```

- [x] All 14 new tests pass (7 for port parsing, 7 for forward command)
- [x] Full test suite passes (799 tests)
- [x] Ruff check and format pass

author: marianfe
body:
Fixes #7896

## Summary

When a Ledger device is unplugged/replugged during a Hardhat session, subsequent signing operations would fail because the plugin kept trying to use a stale connection.

This PR adds automatic reconnection logic that:
- Detects `DisconnectedDevice` and `DisconnectedDeviceDuringOperation` errors from the transport layer
- Closes the stale transport and clears the cached connection
- Reconnects and retries the operation (once)

Added unit tests. This required updating the mock to enable introducing connection failures after a given number of calls. Also manually tested to ensure the fix works as expected. 

Note: `LockedDeviceError` cases are for now handled by existing code, which shows a user-friendly error asking to unlock the device and try again. Will address handling this in a subsequent PR.

author: nilleiz
body:
### Motivation
- The build was failing with `curl` exit code 22 due to an incorrect/unstable Ludusavi release asset URL/filename, so the install must be made robust so CI succeeds on `linux/amd64`.
- Ensure Ludusavi is reproducibly pinned via `LUDUSAVI_VERSION` and ends up as an executable at `/usr/local/bin/ludusavi` on the image PATH.

### Description
- Updated `steam/Dockerfile` to construct the release URL from `LUDUSAVI_VERSION` and try common archive extensions (`tar.xz`, then `tar.gz`) using `curl -fL` and printing the resolved URL on failure.
- Extract the downloaded archive into a temp directory, locate the `ludusavi` binary, and `install -m 0755` it to `/usr/local/bin/ludusavi` so path and permissions are guaranteed.
- Added a build-time sanity check `RUN ludusavi --version` to fail the build early if the binary is missing or broken, and retained `TARGETARCH` mapping (`amd64 -> x86_64`, `arm64 -> aarch64`).
- Documented the `LUDUSAVI_VERSION` build argument in `steam/README.md` and how to pin the release using `docker build --build-arg`.

### Testing
- No automated tests were run; the updated Dockerfile/README will be validated by the next GitHub Actions build (CI) which will exercise the `linux/amd64` image build.
